sections.h2: What makes Pickens County, Georgia, different for a home seller?
sections.html:
Pickens County sits in the north Georgia mountains with Jasper as its seat, and it skews older and pricier than its neighbors in this comparison. Census QuickFacts lists 37,167 residents for July 2025, up 11.9 percent from the 2020 estimates base, and 26.8 percent of them are 65 or older. The county covers 232.06 square miles of land at 143.1 people per square mile.

The median owner-occupied home was valued at $332,700 for 2020 to 2024, the highest of the four Georgia counties in the same table, and 81.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent was $1,136. The county issued 277 building permits in 2025, and health care and social assistance receipts reached $222,994 thousand in 2022, more than any of the other three counties except Paulding. Retail sales per capita came to $20,835.

A senior-heavy owner base matters for tax questions, because Pickens County has local exemptions that older owners may already hold. A buyer who loses those exemptions at closing may see a different bill than the seller paid, and sellers who understand that can explain it before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Pickens County?
sections.html:
The Pickens County Tax Commissioner bills, collects and distributes, and also processes motor vehicle registration. The Board of Tax Assessors appraises property, approves exemptions and reviews appeals. The Board of Equalization, appointed by the grand jury, hears the administrative appeal.

Pickens County tax contacts, per the commissioner's website
ItemDetail
Tax Commissioner address1266 E. Church Street, Jasper, GA 30143
Tax Commissioner phone(706) 253-8882

Commissioner office hoursMonday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The commissioner's news box also mentions a drop box that is open around the clock in front of the Administration Building. Payments by credit card carry a 2.60 percent convenience fee, in the office, online or by phone, and e-check payments carry a flat $3.00 fee. Partial payments are accepted, but interest keeps accruing on the unpaid part.

sections.h2: When is Pickens County property tax due, and what happens if it is late?
sections.html:
The commissioner says real estate and business personal property taxes are due on November 15. Mobile and manufactured homes are billed in January and are due April 1. A US Postal Service postmark counts as timely, but a metered postmark does not.

The FAQ page describes the consequences of paying late:

  • Interest of 0.8750 percent was added for 2025 bills, and from January 2026 the rate is prime plus 3 percent divided across 12 months.
  • A 5 percent penalty is added after 120 days, and the news box says the penalty repeats every 120 days up to a 20 percent cap.
  • After more than 90 days unpaid, a lien (a FIFA) is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, which credit bureaus can read.
  • The commissioner may levy on the property, which the office calls a last resort.

Bills go to the homeowner and never to the mortgage company, so a seller with an escrow account should forward the bill to the lender. If you sell near the due date, ask whether the lender already paid.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Pickens County assessment?
sections.html:
An appeal must be filed within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. It goes first to the Board of Tax Assessors, which reviews its value and tells you its decision. If you are still dissatisfied, the appeal is forwarded to the Board of Equalization for a hearing, and Superior Court is the last step after that.

Some details from the commissioner's general information page:

  • You can appeal on taxability, value, uniformity compared with similar property, or the denial of an exemption.
  • Arbitration is available in place of the Board of Equalization, and you choose it when you file.
  • Returns are filed with the Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1, and a new return that states a different value can set up your appeal rights if the board changes it again.
  • Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, and the millage rate is set by the county commissioners and the Board of Education.

Ask the assessors for the exact mailing date on your notice, since the 45 days count from that date and not from the day it reaches you.

sections.h2: What exemptions can a Pickens County homeowner use?
sections.html:
The standard homestead exemption is $2,000 deducted from the 40 percent assessed value, and it applies to the county, school and state maintenance and operation levies. Applications go to the Board of Tax Assessors, and the county's books close on April 1. An application received after that applies to the next year, and first-time homeowners should bring a copy of the warranty deed.

The commissioner's page lists several age and service exemptions:

  • A local exemption that gives owners 62 or older with gross household income of $25,000 or less a total exemption from school tax on the assessed value.
  • A standard elderly school exemption of up to $10,000 for owners 62 or older whose net income does not exceed $10,000.
  • A general elderly exemption of up to $4,000 for owners 65 or older under the same income limit.
  • A disabled veteran exemption of up to $50,000 of assessed value.
  • A property tax deferral for owners 62 or older with gross household income of $15,000 or less.

The floating exemption, available to owners 62 or older with income of $30,000 or less, replaces other state and county exemptions, and the county warns it can raise a bill at first. Ask the assessors before applying for it.

sections.h2: How should I handle property tax when selling a Pickens County house?
sections.html:
Call the commissioner at (706) 253-8882 for a payoff on the parcel, and ask whether any prior-year balance, interest or lien notice is attached. The commissioner's site has a tax sale page with procedures and a bidder registration form, which tells you how the office handles properties that stay delinquent.

Your sale contract and the closing attorney decide how the year's tax is split. If the seller held an elderly or local school exemption, the buyer starts without it and must apply for a homestead on the new home. A copy of a warranty deed comes from the Clerk of Superior Court in the Pickens County Courthouse.

Mobile homes on the lot are billed in January with an April 1 due date and need a current decal, which is issued when the tax is paid. If a mobile home sits on the lot, ask the commissioner whether it carries a separate bill before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: What is the Pickens County property tax due date?
faqs.a: November 15 for real estate and business personal property, according to the commissioner's pages. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How can I pay a Pickens County tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay in the office by check, cash or card, online by card or e-check, or in the 24-hour drop box. Card payments carry a 2.60 percent fee and e-checks a flat $3.00.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal in Pickens County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. The appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors first, then to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

faqs.q: Does a Pickens County homeowner need to reapply for homestead after buying?
faqs.a: Yes. A new owner or a new residence needs a new application, filed with the assessors by April 1 to count for the same tax year.

faqs.q: Does late Pickens County property tax hurt my credit?
faqs.a: It can. After more than 90 days unpaid, a lien is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, and the commissioner states that credit bureaus may use these public records.
